title: M166 · R2: the navgrid tool checked on your real 16.21 grid
summary: The navgrid tool read the grid from your Wednesday PC run on brain. Every byte of the file is accounted for: v7.1, 295 × 296 cells of 50 units, all seven region layers, the height samples and the hint nodes. The flag bits are settled against the grid's own terrain layer and your game's 81 structure events: 0x01 brush, 0x02 not passable, 0x04 structure footprint (turrets, inhibitors, nexus, fountain), 0x40 see-through, and 0x400/0x800 the blue-only and red-only base gates. 0x80 and 0x1000 stay unnamed. Validation passes: 28 of 28 structures and 81 of 81 timeline events, each within 2 cells and in its lane. With the axes swapped the lane match drops to 8 of 24, which confirms the axis convention. The vectoriser writes valid polygons with every hole kept. Brush keeps 98–99 % of its area, and every boundary is within 9.4 units of the cells. The real file exposed four defects (gates read as walls, structures in the transparent layer, a missing Baron pit, lane checks skipped on nexus turrets). All four are fixed and covered by synthetic tests: 64 pass. Nothing derived from the grid is in git or on this card; it stays in one folder on brain, outside every repo. Report: REPORT-R2.md.

questions.text: Merge the navgrid tool into main (code and synthetic tests only). This touches only tools/navgrid/, .gitignore and the mission folder, and no app code. The ticket-2 rule stays in force: nothing derived from the real grid is committed, shipped or shared until Riot answers.

chips.label: Yes, merge
chips.consequence: After the R2 verifier's PASS, the overseer lands mission/M166-scout-half-c-and-navgrid-prep into main.

chips.label: Not yet
chips.consequence: The branch stays open, and the tool keeps working from it on brain.

questions.recommend: Yes, merge. The real file parses byte-exact, every check passes, and the four defects it exposed are fixed with tests.
